answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 18 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The orchard multiplier is published, charged in voyage, and jade lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4125 identities would post 1206 proofs and burn roughly 87 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
